Reject a missing command or required credential bindings before allocation; do not bake provider-specific arguments into Literate AI. A configured provisioner receives exact target profile, declarative requirements, source-authority inputs, total deadline, and an idempotency key before an `ExecutionDispatchRequest` is created. Its bounded response returns one exact SSH worker descriptor plus opaque lease/recovery identity. Validate the returned worker and requirements, then construct and execute the existing canonical SSH lifecycle request without identity rewriting. Persist no private endpoint or lease data in project authority.

Import the out-of-band artifact/evidence manifest and bundle under controller custody, verify declared identities, byte sizes, worker/request binding, and immutable references, and emit a typed custody receipt before authorizing stop. Missing, corrupt, oversized, timed-out, or ambiguous evidence retains the lease and a recoverable operator status; delete remains a separate explicit action. One total timeout budget must cover provisioning, readiness, execution, transfer, verification, and cleanup.

The same 16 lifecycle cells fail before source evidence: Linux reports `rebuild.standard_distribution_unavailable` because the installed framework payload omits package, policy, or schema authority; Windows reports `project.source_intelligence_command_unavailable` because the required CodeGraph 1.1.1+ command is absent from the isolated worker environment. These are historical failures in an explicitly configured downstream project, not a universal framework prerequisite. ADR 0019 leaves provider installation with its operator. Preserve required-policy refusal and verify the configured executable and current evidence without adding a framework-owned companion package or weakening the selected policy.

Add installed-real-wheel, worker-equivalent Linux and Windows regressions that execute the lifecycle through Standard distribution resolution. Cover a default-none project without an indexer and an explicitly required project with its operator-provided command. Contract tests must reject mismatched worker, request, lease, artifact, evidence, and custody identities; prove retry does not duplicate allocation or destructive cleanup; prove unknown SSH keys and insufficient observed hardware block execution; and prove evidence is imported and verified before default stop. The installed-wheel public CLI proof must run one LitAI project lifecycle through the provisioned SSH worker and leave no unclassified residual. Synthetic fixtures alone do not establish cloud support.

Repair Windows-native tests and behavior for source executable intent, accepted manifest identity, working-tree guard discovery, diagnostic-tail preservation, and projected C++ execution without weakening digest, path, or rollback checks. The first extraction slice now centralizes literal endpoint validation, noninteractive SSH/SCP argv construction, connection/operation timeouts, process termination, bounded output/diagnostics, and stable unavailable/timeout errors in a framework adapter consumed by the fan-out harness. Fifty-eight focused SSH, fan-out, and dispatch tests pass with two intentional platform skips. The next slice is a typed source-materialization envelope followed by the request/result remote lifecycle handler itself. The current dispatch request binds source content but deliberately has no Git-revision or archive-transfer locator, so an SSH handler cannot safely materialize that content without guessing. Add a closed, identity-bound choice between an exact Git repository/revision and a caller-staged archive; never derive transport authority from the worker's mutable checkout. The versioned envelope is now implemented as separate transport authority: it binds the exact dispatch request and extracted source-tree identity, admits only a 40/64-character Git object ID plus credential-free repository URL or the fixed caller-staged archive locator plus its byte identity, and rejects mixed modes, moving refs, file paths, queries, fragments, and embedded HTTPS credentials. Thirty-one focused contract/schema tests pass. The in-progress adapter slice will stage the current project as the archive form, invoke a packaged `litai worker execute` receiver (never a framework-checkout script), and retain artifacts in a worker-local content-addressed store for a later exact-worker run. A reconstruction audit also found that semantic Component/source/Flavor digests alone cannot tell the receiver which target or project-relative Component to invoke. The v2 dispatch request now carries and identity-binds the exact target profile, ordered Flavor selectors, and canonical project-relative Component path; all constructors move forward together with no legacy default. Fifty-five focused contract, schema, CLI, dispatcher, and artifact-export tests pass. The canonical remote source guard is now an installed, stdlib-only module that remains directly executable when uploaded before the transferred project is trusted or importable. The repository script is only a developer launcher, and Git/archive fan-out hashes and executes the installed-module source path. This preserves a single implementation of portable path validation, symlink confinement, archive/Git identity verification, and timeout supervision. All 59 source-guard, fan-out, and SSH transport tests pass with two platform-native skips. The controller archive-capture adapter now inventories only Git-visible or explicitly filtered authored files, excludes credentials ignored by Git and all derived `_build`/index/cache state, detects source mutation during capture, emits deterministic gzip/tar bytes, and binds the request, extracted tree, and transport-byte identities in the materialization envelope. Three focused tests prove exact extraction parity, ignored/derived exclusion, and no-overwrite staging behavior. The receiver/SSH mutation half remains in progress. The local receiver/controller composition now stages exactly four canonical files after one bounded setup, invokes the installed internal `litai worker execute` receiver, verifies archive bytes and extracted tree, drives the existing Standard rebuild boundary without recursive worker selection, persists accepted products plus execution commands in a worker-local content-addressed store, and resolves only that exact digest for `run`.
